reason: All differences follow the request: values p1-p4 accepted and old values rejected on create; due_date offsets 1/3/7/30 (e.g. #4 p2 moved 7->3 days); migration maps urgent->p1, normal->p2/p3, low->p4; claiming p1/p2 is now 403 even where it was 409, and the UI claim action is hidden for them; other changes are only the relabelled priority values.

Rules match the request. Supervisors are limited to their own site for work-order read/assign/cancel/PATCH/create and for asset/part create/PATCH/DELETE, with 403 winning over 400/409. Staff writes are manager-only. Sofia is migrated to manager and shows no loss of rights. Every listed difference is a site-scope 403, a reduced list/UI row set, or the role relabel; no unrequested change.

books.status.computed was changed from l.book == record to l.book != record, which the request did not ask for. Available books now show status on_loan (GET /api/books/2 available->on_loan, even a newly created book), and 231 borrows go 200->409 because the guard requires status available. This breaks borrowing generally, not just for members with overdue loans.

books.status.computed now returns on_loan_x instead of on_loan (e.g. GET /api/books/1 status on_loan -> on_loan_x). That breaks the existing status value and the hold guard, which checks status == on_loan: placing a hold on books that are on loan now gives 409 (POST /api/books/1/hold 404->409) instead of creating a hold. The reserved status is never produced either.

Copy availability is wrong. Every book shows available_copies=0, including books 1 and 22, which should be available through their second copies. Books that were available and have one copy not on loan now show on_loan (GET /api/books/2 status available->on_loan with available_copies=0). As a result, 231 borrows of available books go 200->409 and the UI borrow form disappears (UI /ui/books/2 actions ['borrow'] -> []).
